title: Extrema of Trigonometric Functions on an Interval
quickIdea: For a periodic function restricted to an interval, list the critical points that lie inside, then compare them with the endpoint values - the periodicity does the rest.
remember: sin x has derivative cos x, which vanishes at pi/2 + k pi; f''(x) = -sin x classifies them: pi/2 + 2k pi are maxima, 3pi/2 + 2k pi are minima.
cos x has derivative -sin x, which vanishes at k pi; maxima at 0 + 2k pi and minima at pi + 2k pi.
On a restricted interval only the critical points inside it are candidates, and the endpoints must be evaluated separately.
Values repeat with period 2pi, so an interval longer than 2pi contains the same extremum values more than once - but they are distinct points.
Half-open intervals such as [pi/4, 7pi/4) remove the right endpoint from the candidate list, which can change the answer.

example.prompt: GATE CSE 2012 Q.9: where are the local minima of sin x on [pi/4, 7pi/4]?
example.work: cos x = 0 at pi/2 and 3pi/2, both inside the interval. -sin(pi/2) = -1 < 0 so pi/2 is a local maximum; -sin(3pi/2) = 1 > 0 so 3pi/2 is a local minimum with value -1. Endpoint values: sin(pi/4) = sqrt(2)/2 = 0.707 and sin(7pi/4) = -0.707.
example.answer: The interior local minimum is at 3pi/2; under the endpoint convention pi/4 is a second local minimum, which is the accepted option (two, at pi/4 and 3pi/2).

gateAngle: This is the trigonometric instance of the closed-interval candidate list, and 2012 Q.9 is its only verified CSE appearance. The exam's distractors are the interior point alone (one minimum) and the pair pi/2, 3pi/2 (confusing the maximum with a minimum).

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 2012 Q.9: the number and locations of the local minima of sin x on [pi/4, 7pi/4].
variations.why: One interior minimum plus the left endpoint, under the endpoint convention.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: Where are the local maxima of cos x on [0, 2pi]?
variations.answer: At 0 and at 2pi, both endpoints, each with value 1.
variations.why: A periodic function on a full period puts its maximum exactly at both ends, which makes the endpoint convention unavoidable.

trap.what: Listing pi/2 as a local minimum because cos x = 0 there.
trap.why: A zero of the derivative is a candidate, not a verdict; at pi/2 the sign of cos goes from positive to negative, which is a maximum.
trap.counterexample: sin(pi/2) = 1 is the largest value of sin anywhere, so pi/2 cannot be a local minimum.

check.question: How many local minima does sin x have on [0, 2pi]?
check.explanation: The only interior critical point with positive second derivative is 3pi/2. The endpoints 0 and 2pi both have value 0, which is larger than sin(3pi/2) = -1, so neither is a minimum.
